title: GH#1020: Kadence query loops skip the full REST API boot, theme mods decoded once; release 1.3.99
body:
## Summary

Two Kadence costs paid on every front-end page, fixed in **Fixes for other plugins** (on by default), and release 1.3.99.

- **Kadence Blocks Pro query loops** no longer boot the whole REST API. While a `kadence/query-*` block whose query has not run renders (no REST server running yet), `$wp_rest_server` is a `SEOProStack_Kadence_Query_Server` (new `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-query-server.php`) holding only `GET /wp/v2/kadence_query/query`, with Kadence's own callback, `permission_callback` and args. Kadence's own `rest_do_request()` dispatches there. The global is cleared as dispatch starts and after every block, so any other route or later REST use gets the full server. REST requests are untouched.
- **Kadence theme mods** are decoded once per request: `pre_option_theme_mods_{stylesheet}` (Kadence or a child theme) returns the value decoded once per site and stored string in `wp_load_alloptions()`, through `option_{name}` filters as `get_option()` does.

Not fixable here: Kadence Blocks 3.8.0 design tokens read `wp_kb_design_tokens` 268 times per page (`Token_Store` is `final`, and its DB layer has no short-circuit filter).

## Evidence

Web-SAPI profile, Burnaby network site `/service/construction-company/` (WooCommerce, MCP Adapter, Fluent apps, Ultimate Multisite), three alternating A/B pairs using the same mechanism as a request-local prototype:

| | Query block (inclusive) | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|

## What

New, on by default: **Links skip redirects** (Links tab). Links in posts, block widgets and menus to an old address that Rank Math permanently redirects to another page of the same site now point straight at that page when it is shown. Saved content is unchanged.

Resolves #1046

## Why

Renamed pages keep their old address through Rank Math → Redirections, but internal links still point at it, so each visit and crawl takes an extra 301. A client site did this with a must-use plugin no update reaches; this is the generic version.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-redirect-links.php` (`SEOProStack_Redirect_Links`, key `redirect_links`), listed in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES` after Modal links.

- Front end: `the_content` and `widget_block_content` (`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`) and `wp_nav_menu_objects`, priority 20. Follows chains up to five hops and keeps fragments. Links with a query string are skipped, and HTML that mentions no old path is not parsed.

title: GH#1039: Load plugins only where needed checks each address and skips what it renders the same without; release 1.3.108
body:
Resolves #1039

## What

Load plugins only where needed skips more plugins on each address of the site. Plugins that add something to pages loaded on every page of their kind, even where they added nothing. Each address visitors open is now checked once in the background, and skips only the plugins it renders exactly the same without.

The first approach on this issue, verifying per page kind from sampled pages, failed on a test site: sampled pages had no form, so Fluent Forms was marked safe for every page, and the contact page lost its form (see the issue comment). This PR checks each address by itself instead of generalising from a sample.

## How

- `learn_front()` saves for each page kind the plugins it might also skip (`propose`): plugins that add to pages or extend one that does, but not the kind's needs, plugins that always load or check logins, or **Always load these plugins on the site**.
- `start_front()` keys a cookie-free address by its path plus `cpage`, `p`, `page`, `page_id` and `paged` (search results are not checked). It applies the saved skip set for that address, or queues it after a 200 render (at most 50 queued).
- The scheduled task `seoprostack_front_verify` (`includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`) renders each queued address through a loopback: first as it is served, then without groups of the proposed plugins, halving a group when the page changes.
  - Each render carries a one-time token (`hash_equals`), is kept out of page caches (`DONOTCACHEPAGE` plus a unique argument), never learns or flags the site, and reports which plugin wrote to the database, sent a request or sent mail.
  - Plugins with such effects are never skipped, and a trial that adds effects fails.
  - A match needs the same status, key headers and cookie names, and the same normalised HTML. Up to 50 words that change on every render are tolerated, found by a second base render.
- Results go in `seoprostack_plugin_front_pages`. They hold until the content revision or the plugin set changes, for a week at most, and cover up to 5,000 addresses with shared skip sets. Five loopback failures in a row pause checks for an hour.
- The status panel shows how many addresses were checked, how many skip more plugins and how many wait. Uninstall removes the new options and the hook.

## Verification

On an isolated copy of a production site (45 active plugins, LiteSpeed, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.106 plus these files):

- 17 addresses were queued from visits and all were verified across 4 scheduled runs (about 50 s each). Single pages, the contact page, the home page, archives and pagination were among them.
- Cookie-free HTML compared with and without the saved checks was identical on all 17 addresses, apart from LiteSpeed's timestamp comments.
- Plugins loaded per page:

| Pages | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single pages | 36 | 20 |
| Contact page (keeps Fluent Forms; form present) | 36 | 22 |
| Archives | 39 | 34 |

- Server time to headers (median of 4 interleaved rounds):

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single page | about 620 ms | about 400 ms |
| Home | 531 ms | 441 ms |
| Directory archive | 540 ms | 535 ms |

- A search URL was not queued.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs and phpstan all pass.

title: GH#1061: WebP and AVIF images records a conversion only when the picture is unchanged; release 1.3.115
body:
## Summary

WebP and AVIF images could mark a picture converted while WordPress was still making its sizes, with a record (`_seoprostack_nextgen`) missing the later sizes. Media in cloud storage uploads only listed copies, so those copies stayed on the server, never sent or uploaded, and a storage drain with local removal on could not finish. Release 1.3.115.

Resolves #1061

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
  - `GENERATION` post meta (`_seoprostack_nextgen_generation`), changed by `metadata_updated()` on every metadata save.
  - `convert_attachment()` reads the generation from the database before the sizes, and `unchanged()` compares generation, attached file and file names at the end. A change leaves the picture waiting (`nextgen_changed`); the next conversion keeps the copies made and lists every size.
  - `run_batch()` defers `nextgen_changed` pictures to the next batch; `wp seoprostack convert-images` passes over pictures that stay waiting after an error once per run (it could repeat them before).
  - `record_unlisted()`: converts a converted picture again when up-to-date copies of its files are missing from its record. The skip conditions match `convert_attachment()`'s loop, so a conversion always lists what it flags.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: `upload_attachment()` calls `record_unlisted()` after restoring removed files; when it changed the record, the picture is queued (which clears the retry job) and uploaded with its copies by the next batch.

| Converted again | lists new size | lists new size, copy on disk |

title: GH#1064: Media in cloud storage names uploads from the claim index, not every stored record; release 1.3.117
body:
## Summary

With local copies removed, every `wp_unique_filename()` call read every stored inventory of the site (`stored_records()`) to list the folder's stored names. Production directory stacks paid 0.27s (1,385 stored pictures), 2.92s (15,221) and 7.24s (18,949) per call, several calls per picture, so bulk imports slowed as libraries grew.

WordPress only tests names that begin with the file name's stem (without a trailing `-N`): `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` matches `{name}-(size|scaled|rotated){ext}` case-insensitively, for the name, its numbers and other formats. So:

- `index_claims()` also stores a name claim (`n:{folder}\n{prefix}`) for each stored file under every hyphen-ended prefix of its lower-case name and the whole name (`name_hashes()`), in the existing `seoprostack_media_claims` table. The index is rebuilt for each version already, so no schema change.
- `unique_filename_files()` computes the stem (`numbering_stem()`), reads only the inventories under its claim (`stem_records()`: one primary-key lookup, then `handover_records()`), and returns only names beginning with the stem, local `scandir()` names included.
- Until the index is complete for this version, or when the lookup fails (`claims_failed()`), it streams every inventory as before, still filtered by stem.

Version 1.3.117 (plugin header, constant, readme, README, changelog).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Read-only equivalence check on production inventories (the branch's `numbering_stem()`/`name_hashes()` logic copied into a `wp eval-file` script, index simulated from every inventory): 3 stacks, 34,669 inventories, 846,160 names in this month's folder, 243 sample upload names (stored stems as uploaded, numbered, upper-case, size-like, other formats, new names); every name the full list holds for a stem was found through the index, and 15,480 `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` tests gave the same answer with the full and the index-scoped list.
